According
uh-KORD-ing
p.pr. (with to)
From accord: Latin ad + cor, heart, then Old French acorder, to bring heart to heart, to agree. Webster 1828: agreeing, harmonizing; suitable, in accordance with; always followed by to; never a bare preposition. The KJV’s ordinary theological phrase is according to — measured by a standard that is not the speaker.

Biblical Definition

According in Scripture names the rule something is measured by. Salvation is not according to us: Who hath saved us, and called us with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace (2 Tim 1:9). Election has the same meter: the called are those who love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose (Rom 8:28); we were predestinated according to the good pleasure of his will (Eph 1:5). Sanctification has a written rule: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word (Ps 119:9). Judgment has a written rule too: the dead are judged according to their works (Rev 20:12). The word therefore refuses two modern instincts at once. It will not let the sinner be saved according to his record, and it will not let the saint walk according to his feelings. Grace elects according to purpose; the Word cleanses according to itself; the last day renders according to deeds. Those are not three religions. They are one God, measuring three moments by three of His own standards — purpose, Word, and works as evidence — never by the sinner’s self-report.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines ACCORDING as agreeing, harmonizing; suitable, agreeable, in accordance with. It has its true participial sense, agreeing, and is always followed by to. It is never a preposition.

expand to see more

ACCORDING, p.pr. — Agreeing; harmonizing. Th’ according music of a well mixt state.

ACCORDING, p.pr. — Suitable; agreeable; in accordance with. Our zeal should be according to knowledge. Webster insists the word agrees with a sentence, is always followed by to, and is never a preposition.

Key Scripture

Romans 8:28 — "And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose."

Ephesians 1:5 — "Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will,"

2 Timothy 1:9 — "Who hath saved us, and called us with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began,"

Psalm 119:9 — "Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word."

Revelation 20:12 — "And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works."

Modern Corruption

According is corrupted when “my truth” and private self-report replace God’s purpose and Word as the measure, when election is recast as according to foreseen faith, and when cheap grace pretends the last day will not judge according to works as evidence.

expand to see more

The age’s favorite standard is the self. “Live according to your truth.” “According to my story.” Scripture will not take that meter. A young man cleanses his way according to the Word, not according to the heart (Ps 119:9; Jer 17:9). The recovery is to restore the object of to: purpose, good pleasure, Word, mercy — God’s, not ours.

The second corruption is synergistic election. Semi-Pelagian and decisionist schemes make calling according to foreseen faith or according to the sinner’s yes. Second Timothy 1:9 shuts that door: not according to our works, but according to His own purpose and grace, given in Christ Jesus before the world began. Conditional election is not a humble reading of Romans 8:28. It is a different according-to.

The third corruption is antinomian abuse of the same grace. If salvation is not according to works, the flesh concludes that the last day will not be according to works either. Revelation 20:12 forbids that. Justification is by imputed righteousness, received by faith alone. Judgment still opens books. Works are not the ground of acceptance; they are the public evidence of what grace made. Rome confuses the two and justifies by works. Cheap grace confuses the two and empties the books. The Reformed confession keeps both texts.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

From accord (Latin ad + cor, heart; Old French acorder). Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek kata (G2596) at Rom 8:28, Eph 1:5, 2 Tim 1:9, Rev 20:12. Psalm 119:9 tags Hebrew dābār (H1697) on thy word, not a separate Hebrew for English according; no number is invented for the English prepositional phrase.

expand to see more

Greek kata (G2596) — down from, according to, after (Rom 8:28; Eph 1:5; 2 Tim 1:9; Rev 20:12).

Hebrew dābār (H1697) — word, matter (Ps 119:9, according to thy word — tagged on the noun, not invented as a Hebrew for the English participle).

English according to — Webster: participial, always with to; the KJV’s ordinary meter-phrase for purpose, Word, grace, and judgment.

Usage

"Called according to his purpose — election’s meter is God’s good pleasure, not the sinner’s record."

"Cleanse the way according to thy word — the standard is written, not felt."

"The dead are judged according to their works — evidence at the last day, not a second gospel."
